page: Microsoft Azure DC32s_v3 is a member of the DCSv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, resulting in 1.0 thread per core. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or bundled GPU, but the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Multi-core performance is a primary strength of this instance. Benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench, alongside a strong Passmark CPU score of 49792.6. Cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities are also strong, with Passmark CPU encryption reaching 36894.88. Single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1686.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1897.99. Memory bandwidth tests show average results, such as 166.76 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

The server exhibits strong capabilities in database operations, scoring 25003.69 in Passmark database benchmarks, and static web serving throughput at 47.09 GB/sec. However, text generation on large language models is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation benchmark falling into the weak category at 2.73 tokens/sec. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong multi-threaded performance, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, while being less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation.
description: Microsoft Azure DC32s_v3 is an x86_64 server in the DCSv3 family, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 32 vCPUs, and 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a Passmark CPU score of 49792.6 and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations and static web serving throughput are also strong. Conversely, single-core performance and large-scale LLM text generation are average to weak, with 70B model text generation dropping to 2.73 tokens/sec. This qualitative resource density makes the server highly suitable for memory-optimized workloads, database management, and multi-threaded processing, while presenting a tradeoff in single-threaded efficiency and heavy AI inference tasks.
